html:
Ruanda-Urundi was the territory of Rwanda and Burundi ruled by Belgium from 1916, when Belgian troops took it from German East Africa, until independence in 1962.

Belgium ruled through the Tutsi chiefs of the monarchies, removing Hutu chiefs and treating the Tutsi as a separate, superior race, a view shared by the Catholic missions that ran the schools. In the 1930s it gave everyone an identity card stating their group. Farmers were forced to grow coffee.

In the 1950s Belgium switched its support to the Hutu majority. The identity cards survived independence, and in 1994 they were used at roadblocks to choose who would die in the genocide.
sum: Ruanda-Urundi was the territory of Rwanda and Burundi ruled by Belgium from 1916, when Belgian troops took it from German East Africa, until independence in 1962.
